title: Ensure idempotent billing for at-least-once request paths
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Background:
Redwood's ingestion and billing surfaces must avoid double-counting tokens/requests when clients or intermediate proxies retry requests. We currently have several at-least-once ingestion paths (hosted API ingress, dedicated capacity frontends, internal queue replays) that can lead to duplicate usage records when retries/timeouts occur. This ticket designs and implements an idempotency-first layer for billing-safe ingestion and documents the trade-offs for latency, correctness, and cross-region traffic.

Goals:
- Guarantee no user-visible double-billing for common retry scenarios (network retry from client, 504->retry, gateway replay) within a configurable dedupe window (default 24h).
- Minimize additional latency on the hot request path (target <2ms extra median).
- Preserve rate-limiting semantics: retries should not circumvent client-rate quotas or burst behavior.
- Provide robust observability and alerts for dedupe failures and storage pressure.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change long-term invoicing/billing reconciliation processes (accounting exports). It focuses on real-time usage ingestion correctness.

Proposed design (summary):
1) Idempotency token surface: require or accept an Idempotency-Key header for idempotent operations; if absent, generate a strong request fingerprint at the gateway using stable fields (API key, model, prompt hash, client timestamp) and attach as X-RW-Idempotency-Fingerprint.
2) Dedupe store: use a Redis cluster (replicated across AZs) for fast dedupe lookups with small TTLs (configurable per-route). Keys are prefixed by account_id:route:token. Value is a compact metadata blob (dedupe-status flag, billed_units, accepted_at, origin-node). To keep JSON-free, billing write stores only a reference id; the actual billing commit is atomic and idempotent-guarded in the billing write path.
3) Two-phase commit for billing write: a cheap local write marks the idempotency key as "processing" and returns quickly; the aggregator workers perform the token accounting and write a final committed record. The dedupe store prevents a second commit within window.
4) Rate-limit interplay: retries will count against request-rate quotas at gateway ingress. For billing quotas (tokens), the first successful commit is billed; retries that reach aggregator after commit will be deduped. If a retry bypasses gateway rate-limit via routing differences, dedupe still prevents double-billing because token commit is guarded by idempotency key.
5) Cross-region/HA: to avoid cross-region latency, gateways will write a local dedupe entry with usually eventual replication; a forwarder will check remote status if local TTL is missing and the request looks like a duplicate. We accept a small race in cross-region scenarios for extremely short windows but will widen dedupe window for high-risk accounts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Synchronous global dedupe store vs local-first with replication: chosen local-first to preserve latency and availability; accept small duplication risk for very short windows in cross-region failures.
- Memory footprint vs TTL correctness: default 24h window for correctness; provide per-account override and probabilistic sharded bloom filters for very high-volume customers to limit memory.
- Strong idempotency-key requirement vs ease-of-use: support both client-supplied keys (recommended) and fingerprint fallback. Document best practices in the API docs.

Acceptance criteria:
- New idempotency layer is enabled behind feature flag for 10% of accounts and shows zero double-billing incidents in that cohort across a 2-week test window (manual validation + automated diff of accounting exports).
- Median added latency at gateway < 2ms when feature enabled in local region; p95 < 8ms.
- Observability: dashboards for dedupe hit/miss rate, storage memory usage, eviction rate, and a Grafana alert for dedupe miss rates increasing >0.1% baseline.
- Integration tests covering: client retry, gateway timeout+retry, aggregator replays, cross-region duplicate within window, and race where two nodes attempt commit simultaneously.

Implementation plan (high-level):
- Phase 1 (2 wks): library and gateway work: idempotency header passthrough, deterministic fingerprint generation, small Redis client and schema, feature-flag gating. Unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2587
- Phase 2 (2 wks): aggregator changes: two-phase commit semantics, idempotency guard in billing writer, accounting export idempotence validation, e2e tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/434
- Phase 3 (2 wks): rollout to 10% accounts, collect telemetry, iterate on TTLs and memory tuning; increase to 50% then 100% after validation.

Monitoring and observability:
- New metrics: dedupe_store_get, dedupe_store_set, dedupe_store_evictions, idempotency_conflicts, billing_commit_attempts, billing_commits_deduped.
- Dashboards: per-route dedupe ratio, per-account anomalies, and a synthetic test that replays a known request then retries to assert no second billed commit.
- Alerts: dedupe_store_evictions > threshold, billing_commits_deduped spike outside baseline, and cross-region replication lag > 500ms for N minutes.

Docs and rollout notes:
- Update API docs with Idempotency-Key usage patterns and examples (Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Idempotency+for+Billing).
- SDKs: add helper to set Idempotency-Key and to allow optional fingerprint fallback.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Redis memory pressure causing evictions and missed dedupe -> mitigation: adaptive TTLs, offload cold keys to Postgres-backed long window store for VIP accounts.
- Risk: mis-specified fingerprint causing false dedupe -> mitigation: conservative fingerprint fields and an allowlist to opt-out for fuzzy detection.

Notes on alternatives considered:
- Use a strong global sequence generator per-account to dedupe: rejected because synchronous global sequence hurts latency and availability for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Use event-sourced ledger and reconcile duplicates post-factum: still needed for billing reconciliation but not sufficient for customer-facing prevention of double-billing.

QA checklist:
- Unit tests for fingerprint generation edge cases (time skew, different encodings).
- Integration tests: run ingress+aggregator in local k8s with Redis and simulate retries and replays.
- Load test: 50k qps dedupe store read/write + eviction behavior.

testing_steps: 1) Run local integration harness: simulate client resend with same Idempotency-Key and confirm single billing commit.
2) Simulate gateway timeout where client retries with new ephemeral connection and no Idempotency-Key: verify fingerprint dedupe prevents second commit within TTL.
3) Cross-region test: send same request to two regions within 200ms and assert dedupe results in only one committed usage record.
4) Failure mode: bring down Redis node and ensure system still serves (best-effort dedupe) and increments a metric for failed dedupe lookups.
notes: Do not rely on client-supplied idempotency keys for critical customers without server-side verification.
For Dedicated/private deployments, document recommended Redis topology in the Private deployment playbook.
